name: Park Hyatt Guangzhou
positioning: High-rise Park Hyatt on the upper floors of Yingkai Square Tower in Zhujiang New Town, near the Pearl River, with Super Potato interiors drawing on Lingnan heritage
best_for: Travelers who want a high-floor city base with views toward Canton Tower and the Pearl River
Business travelers and Canton Fair attendees who value a direct metro connection
Families who want kids menus and children's amenities

facts.text: The hotel sits on the uppermost floors of the Yingkai Square Tower, steps from the Pearl River embankment.
The Yingkai Square tower was designed by Chicago-based architecture firm Goettsch Partners.
The interior design draws on the cultural heritage of the Lingnan region.
Rooms have a marble bathroom with a deep soaking tub with a television, a double vanity and a rain shower.
Yue Jing Xuan serves Cantonese cuisine from an open kitchen.
The Dining Room serves Mediterranean cuisine and Italian wines.
The Living Room offers afternoon tea and curated workshops.
The Spa is bathed in natural light high above the city.
The hotel has kids menus at all venues, and provides baby cribs and kids bathrobes and slippers.
Yue Jing Xuan is listed as Michelin Guide Selected for 2018 to 2026.
Meeting Salons on the 66th floor have floor-to-ceiling windows.

highlights.text: The hotel displays works by Japanese artist Tadashi Kawamata, made from reclaimed wood and inspired by the dragons of Baiyun Mountain.
The interiors are by Tokyo-based design firm Super Potato.
Canton Tower view rooms face south across the Pearl River toward the Canton Tower.
The Roof Bar has an outdoor terrace and live music.
Connecting room pairs share a private entrance foyer set apart from the main guestroom corridor.

considerations.text: Guangzhou Baiyun International Airport is 40 kilometers away, about 45 to 60 minutes by car depending on traffic.
The hotel is directly connected to Zhujiang New Town metro station, and self-parking is in the tower's basement with direct elevator access to the hotel.
WhataHotel notes the business-oriented location may suit leisure travelers less.
